memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All those who went to Egypt with Jacob—those who were his direct descendants, not counting his sons' wives—numbered sixty-six persons. With the two sons who had been born to Joseph in Egypt, the members of Jacob's family, which went to Egypt, were seventy in all." — Gen 46:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seventy people. That is the entire nation of Israel at this point — one extended family that could fit into a large room.

Hold that number next to the promise. God had told Abraham his descendants would be as numerous as the stars and the sand on the seashore (Gen 22:17). Seventy people walking into Egypt does not look like the stars.

But by the time they walk out, four hundred years later, they will be a nation so large that Pharaoh is frightened of them (Ex 1:9-10).

God's promises often look impossibly small in the middle. If you had stood on that road watching seventy dusty travellers, you would have thought the promise was failing. You would have been watching it being fulfilled.

This is why we walk by faith and not by sight (2 Cor 5:7). What God is doing is rarely measurable at the moment we are living through it. The kingdom of God started with a handful of frightened disciples in a locked room, and Jesus told them they would be His witnesses to the ends of the earth.

Do not judge the size of God's work by what you can count today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does God's promise feel too small in your life right now?
2. What would it look like to walk by faith rather than by what you can measure?
3. Has God ever grown something from far less than you expected?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me not to judge Your work by what I can count today. Grow my faith to trust Your promises even when they look impossibly small. Amen.
